question.text: Compliance activities of a trading member in equity derivatives include:

answer.text: KYC, client-broker agreement execution, timely execution of client orders, adequate margin collection, separate client bank account, timely pay-in/pay-out, contract notes, complaint resolution, statements of account, and UCC maintenance
Guaranteeing profits on all client trades
Executing trades without any compliance or risk-disclosure obligation
Sharing proprietary trading strategies with clients

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook lists a trading member's client-related compliance activities as KYC, execution of the client-broker agreement, timely execution of client orders, adequate margin collection, maintaining a separate client bank account, timely pay-in and pay-out of funds and securities, issuing contract notes, resolving client complaints, sending statements of account, and maintaining the Unique Client Code. The workbook also requires the Risk Disclosure Document to be given to derivatives clients. The Trap: Guaranteeing profits or trading without any compliance or risk-disclosure obligation contradicts the workbook list. Sharing proprietary strategies is not a stated client obligation. Note: Use the workbook's compliance checklist as the anchor; do not extend it to a generalised "best interest" standard that is not stated for derivatives brokers.
